text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- UPM-Kymmene's board dropped leading industrialists Casimir Ehrnrooth, Tauno Matomaki and Yrjo Niskanen from the helm of its board, making L.J. Jouhki non-executivce chairman and CEOs Iiro Viinanen of Pohjola and Vesa Vainio of Merita co-chairmen.
- Sanoma Oy to publish a rival to Aamulehti's Kauppalehti business daily, including electronic information services, in November. Core of product is news agency Startel.
- Parliament's planned new building accepted by the City of Helsinki but not by the parliamentary groups.
- Two Finns on skiing expedition across Greenland died of hypothermia but third expedition member was rescued by helicopter, after the trio failed to raise their tent and shelter against the cold.
- Centre Party is already preparing to be in next government, releasing on Thursday a five-point programme with labour reform as a key ingredient.

- An increasing number of Finns are concerned about future income despite current economic upturn, but violence and security issues are seen less threatening than in other European countries, poll shows.

- Hacker broke into Tampere-based Internet service provider SciFi's server last Friday, using a gap in the Unix system to steal passwords. SciFi managing director says the intrusion came from abroad and will likely be traced.
KAUPPALEHTI

- New law about Bank of Finland currently in parliament to include clause that board members must have permission from the parliamentary supervisors for external appointments such as membership of listed companies' boards.
- Interbank managing director Paavo Prepula says risks have fallen and the heaviest burdens are related to claims from state asset management company Arsenal's sphere.
- The state's new defence materials company Patria Industries targets a profit this year.
- Some 45-50 local cooperative banks to remain outside a tigher cooperation around OKOBANK and they are likely to leave the cooperative group.
AAMULEHTI
- Car owners will have to pay two years' car taxes within just a few months since this year's car tax will be collected in the autumn and next year's at the start of the year.
- Investment professionals have not invested much overall in shares and there are only about 20 stock market millionaires in the city community, report based on the insider register shows.
- Baltic Sea has started recovering from pollution, says German professor Dietwart Nehring who has studied the sea for 30 years.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Radical restructuring of the economy will be needed in case of a downturn, opposition leader, Centre Party chairman Esko Aho writes in column.
DEMARI
- Tens of thousands of members of the Confederation of Salaried Employees in Finland (STTK) may participate in planned strike against a government plan to raise some womens' retirement age.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Stormy weather expected.
- Surly people are ego-centric and every civilised human has an obligation to maintain a good mood, says body language expert and actor Asko Sarkola.
-- Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 242, news@reuters.fi
